derivation: active participle of an imaginary denominative from H3754 (כֶּרֶם);
kjv: vine dresser (as one or two words).

occurrences.text: But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.

Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry.
But Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard left certain of the poor of the land for vinedressers and for husbandmen.
Be ye ashamed, O ye husbandmen; howl, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; because the harvest of the field is perished.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
